item.title: Canary - v2.3.5 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
* Fixed a bug in the AutoRefresh module where a refreshEvery longer than about 24 days overflowed the browser's timer and refreshed continuously instead of waiting. * CSS fixes for padding and font consistency across Canary's core 'form element' modules - TextField, Pulldown, CheckboxPulldown and TimePicker. Some of this is in response to recent shifts in Chrome's own CSS defaults and rendering. * Pages in the Sideview UI now print cleanly. On paper they drop the navigation and on-screen controls, tables print every row, side-by-side panels each get the full width of the page, and dark-theme pages print as dark text on white. * The SearchControls module can now be configured with only its print button and placed anywhere in a view, for example in the page header. Its print button also no longer looks disabled before a search has run. * Fixed a bug where a 401 that logging in again could not fix sent the browser into an endless login redirect loop. * Fixed a bug where Table and Chart kept saying the search was still running after the job was paused. * Fixed a bug on Splunk instances running Python 3.7, where a bad trust store gave a confusing error instead of our message saying so.


Description:
Canary is essentially an alternate User Interface framework for Splunk. It implements its own extensible view creation slash dashboarding system that other apps can use. It is a descendant of the old Sideview Utils (defunct for years now) but whereas Sideview Utils ran on top of Splunk’s “Advanced XML” systems, Canary does not. For a great deal more information about Canary, see our website ( https://sideviewapps.com/documentation/canary ) NOTE: This app runs in python3 without any problems and without any changes required. Splunk's "Upgrade Readiness App" may erroneously state that our apps do not run in python3 but it is wrong and please contact us if you have any questions about this.

item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Provides compliance dashboards, maturity model assessments, and THIRF objective tracking aligned to OMB Memorandum M-26-14 federal logging requirements for federal agencies.


Description:
The Carbon 9 Defense - Compliance App extends federal logging compliance coverage for OMB Memorandum M-26-14, which governs effective and efficient agency logging and network visibility to defend against evolving cyber threats. The app provides compliance dashboards, maturity model assessments, and Threat Hunting and Incident Response Framework (THIRF) objective tracking aligned to M-26-14 requirements. It operates as a soft companion to Compliance Essentials for Splunk, sharing compatible data structures but requiring no hard dependency. The app uses three KV store collections to track systems inventory, manual attestation scores, and configuration parameters, alongside two CSV lookups that map systems to expected sourcetypes and event hosts to system identifiers. Four saved searches compute Inventory Visibility, Collection Coverage, Asset Snapshots, and merged Maturity Scores, enabling automated tracking of compliance posture over time. The app is intended for Compliance Officers managing federal logging posture, SOC Analysts tracking event log coverage and retention, and Federal IT administrators implementing M-26-14 controls.

item.title: IEV Evaluation by August Schell - v1.5.4 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
This release adds new Dashboard Studio dashboards, a settings page, dollar figures, a license eligibility check and Cisco consolidation scenarios. ### New **Dashboard Studio dashboards** * Overview, Opportunities, History, Executive Summary and Cisco Consolidation Scenarios are now Dashboard Studio dashboards, and they are the default. * Executive Summary uses a light theme for clean PDF export. * The classic Simple XML dashboards are still included and linked from the IEV Settings page. **IEV Settings page** * Change every setting on one page and save, with no need to edit search macros. * Includes a helper that works out your annual cost per GB/day from your license cost and size. * Opens on first launch as the app setup page. * Your settings are saved to the app’s local configuration, so they survive upgrades and replicate across a search head cluster. * Saving requires the admin or sc_admin role. **Dollar figures** * Set an annual license cost per GB/day to see estimated annual savings on each dashboard and by index. * While demo mode is on, a sample price of $1,500 per GB/day per year is used until you set your own. **License eligibility check** * Reads your license size from license_usage.log and tells you whether your license qualifies for IEV. * You can set the license type and licensed GB/day yourself when the size can’t be read. * On Splunk Cloud, the check asks you to set your license type rather than guessing. **Cisco Consolidation Scenarios** * Estimates the IEV savings if data from other vendors’ products came from the equivalent Cisco products. * Covers firewall, web proxy and SSE, MFA, network access control, and network infrastructure. * On by default. You can turn it off on the IEV Settings page. **More insight** * Savings by index. * Sourcetypes in the Cisco firewall promotion are shown separately. * Suggested fixes for Cisco data that isn’t landing on an eligible sourcetype. * Every page shows which version of the eligible sourcetype list it uses. **Optional alerts** (off by default) * Eligible Cisco share dropped * New Cisco looking sourcetype not eligible **Look and feel** * New app icon and logo. ### Improved * **Clearer banners:** data source and license banners are shorter and shown at equal width, so the full message is always visible. * **Fuller demo mode:** it now covers the license check, dollar figures and the Consolidation Scenarios page. * **Plainer wording:** all on screen text speaks directly to you. * **More accurate averages:** * Today’s partial day is left out, and days with no data still count. * Dollar totals are worked out before rounding, so they match the per index tables. * **Fuller host views:** in license usage mode, host views include volume the license manager rolled up as “(squashed)”. * **Better Cisco matching:** fewer false matches for Cisco looking sourcetypes. For example, “enterprise” no longer matches “ise”. * **Faster scenarios:** changing a Scenarios dropdown no longer reruns the base search. ### Fixed * **Header logo:** the logo now loads on Dashboard Studio dashboards, and its text is no longer cut off. * **Settings link:** the “Open IEV settings” link now works. Newer Splunk versions rejected it with “Argument ns is not supported”. * **License usage you can’t see:** if your data source is set to license usage but none is visible to you, the banner now says so in amber instead of showing zeros as real data. * **Stale alerts:** the “Eligible Cisco share dropped” alert no longer fires on old history data. * **Settings page:** * Settings that failed to load are never overwritten when you save. * Settings are now saved one at a time. * **First run:** saving the settings with no changes now stops the settings page from opening every time you open the app. * **Custom root path:** links work when Splunk Web runs under a custom root path. ### Upgrade notes * **Settings page on first open:** after upgrading, the app opens the IEV Settings page once. Review your settings and click Save settings. * **Consolidation Scenarios now on:** they are on by default. Turn them off on the IEV Settings page if you don’t want them. * **JavaScript for settings only:** the app now includes JavaScript, used only for the settings page. It still has no Python, no data inputs and no external connections.


Short Description:
See how much of your Splunk ingest is IEV eligible Cisco data, your effective license use at the 0.5x weight, estimated savings, and Cisco data on ineligible sourcetypes.


Description:
IEV Evaluation by August Schell shows what Splunk Integrated Enterprise Value (IEV) for Cisco data is worth in your environment. Under IEV, eligible Cisco data ingested with a supported sourcetype counts at a 0.5x weight against applicable ingest entitlement. Most organizations do not know how much of their ingest qualifies. This app measures it. The app matches your ingest by sourcetype against the list of IEV eligible sourcetypes published by Splunk. It shows actual ingest, eligible Cisco ingest, effective license consumption and estimated savings, overall and by index. Set your annual license cost per GB/day to see savings in dollars. A built in license check tells you whether your license qualifies for IEV. The app also finds Cisco data that is not landing on an eligible sourcetype, with suggested fixes, so you can see value being left on the table before your renewal. Cisco Consolidation Scenarios estimate what IEV would be worth if data from other vendors’ firewall, web proxy and SSE, MFA, network access control and network infrastructure products came from the equivalent Cisco products. Volume can come from license usage (license_usage.log), from an estimate based on tstats event counts and sampled event sizes when license data is not visible, or from built in demo data. Dashboards include Overview, Opportunities, History, an Executive Summary for PDF export, and Consolidation Scenarios. Two optional alerts can tell you if your eligible Cisco share drops or a new Cisco looking sourcetype appears. Change every setting on one settings page. The app runs at search time with no Python, modular inputs, data models or external network calls. The only JavaScript is the settings page, which saves to the app’s own configuration. It works in air gapped and FIPS environments. Results are estimates for planning. Splunk validates eligible usage and determines actual IEV treatment under your order and applicable terms.

item.title: Data Source Watchdog for Splunk - v1.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Initial release. - Sourcetype and host trackers (every 15 minutes, tstats only) with KV store state, plus nightly arrival-gap and hour-of-week volume baselines. - Statuses: SILENT, LATE, FUTURE, LOW_VOLUME and HIGH_VOLUME, with seasonality-aware silence detection. - Dashboards: Overview, Entity Detail, Hosts, Data Quality, Manage and Help. - Four alerts (shipped disabled, no actions) that respect mutes and priority. - Tested on Splunk Enterprise 10.6.


Short Description:
Know when a data source goes quiet: silent sources and hosts, ingestion lag, timestamp problems and volume anomalies, with per-source learned baselines. No setup needed, Splunk Cloud compatible.


Description:
The first time anyone notices that a firewall, an endpoint agent or a cloud feed has stopped sending data is usually the day an investigation needs it. Data Source Watchdog catches that within minutes. Install it on your search head and you are done: no lookups to fill in and no thresholds to guess. Every 15 minutes a lightweight tstats tracker records when each index + sourcetype and each host last delivered data. Every night the app learns what normal looks like for each source - how long its gaps usually are and how many events it sends in each hour of the week. Each source is then flagged as SILENT (no data for longer than its own learned gap, seasonality-aware so business-hours sources do not alarm every night), LATE (ingestion lag above your threshold), FUTURE (events timestamped ahead of now), or LOW_VOLUME / HIGH_VOLUME compared with the same hour in previous weeks. The app also shows silent hosts and forwarders, timestamp-parsing and line-truncation problems per sourcetype with the props.conf fix to apply, a form to mute sources or set priorities and owners, and four ready-made alerts. It is pure SPL and Splunk Cloud compatible: no Python, no custom JavaScript, no inputs and no network calls.

item.title: Cisco DC Networking - v2.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
* Added column sorting throughout product details, related objects, endpoint/path evidence, exact measurements, lifecycle, checkpoint and setup tables, including separate interface Admin and Operational states. Activate a column heading again to reverse direction. Sorting applies to all loaded matching rows before pagination; it does not request extra controller data. Numeric zero remains a value, missing values sort last, and action-only columns remain controls. * Corrected proxy credential URL encoding across product connections, preserving spaces and special characters in outbound authentication while retaining saved account settings. * Improved ACI physical-interface status, units and operational-speed presentation, and connected Overview switch details to the existing Inventory investigations without adding controller requests. * Connected consecutive reported measurements in shared time-series charts regardless of sample spacing. Preserved actual sample markers, series identity, exact values and keyboard selection; missing values are not filled or interpreted as zero. * ACI health and active-fault reads finish when APIC's validated page total proves completion, avoiding a redundant empty request. Changed child populations restart only the pending parent probe; written-page recovery and controller budgets remain intact. * Contract consumer/provider relationships correlate on the observed contract parent DN without assuming a reverse-relation name format. Routing views label node/VRF-sharing L3Outs as configuration context rather than implying a unique peer association. * Endpoint attachment history compares interfaces within each observed node; vPC peer observations are not labelled as endpoint moves. Cross-node migration requires separate source evidence. * Normally completed, count-verified searches accept Splunk's exact reduced-bucket performance notice. Truncation, unknown warnings and abnormal jobs still fail closed. * ACI history classes interrupted by a read timeout yield the next branch turn while retaining checkpoints, controller cooldowns and request limits. * Authentication views exclude collector credential metadata. Learned MAC observations no longer appear as IP addresses through CIM aliases, and zero-result messages apply to both text and field filters. * Fault Type filters retain APIC’s native type from vendor metadata or original JSON instead of Splunk’s normalized event classification. * Corrected ACI tenant/EPG counts to use canonical policy identities, reconciled active faults with indexed faultInst evidence, and added native Severity/Domain/Type filters. ACI views use contextual row actions and account labels while preserving controller identifiers. * Added physical fabricLink topology with observed ports, IP/MAC endpoint search, system-model correlation and per-site firmware distribution. New indexed investigations cover external EPG subnets, contract consumers/providers, node hardware, BGP/OSPF neighbors and PBR/IP SLA evidence. Optional collection stays explicit and missing operational telemetry stays unknown. * ND partial resource batches now include acknowledged output in cycle event totals while retaining incomplete status and resume checkpoints. * Connectivity Analysis now distinguishes authentication timeouts, TLS failures, connection failures and rejected logins from fabric API failures, including errors wrapped by the shared ND login client. Diagnostics never expose credentials or controller response bodies. * Made ND policy retirement reachable from Setup’s disabled-input list and account-deletion guidance. Review reads local retirement evidence without reconnecting every configured controller. Accounts may be removed after a directly created policy’s full retirement proof is verified; disabled safety records and permanent fences remain. Ordinary disabled policies, MDS references and protected migration recovery remain guarded. * Clarified that ND discovery creates related ACI/Nexus 9000 accounts, lists their identities and explains incomplete discovery sources. Search scope retains explicit monitoring destinations before first events and when indexed-data discovery fails, and includes reduced buckets in index discovery. * Fixed the narrow Connectivity Analysis wrapper, switched fabric discovery to the documented inventory summary and added safe connection-error categories. ND IP cells link to scoped Endpoint Search; hosted/outbound protocol values display names and numbers. Traffic categories compare the latest service-list collection against the latest ND summary and explain count mismatches without inventing rates or collection-health failures. * Corrected MDS direct syslog header/timestamp recognition for colon-prefixed messages without a hostname, including optional process text. MDS severity lookups now return one canonical value. Added the SSH/terminal procedure used for a real UDP receiver test, with CFS isolation, verbosity and restoration guidance. New timestamp assignment requires receiver activation; historical event times are unchanged and MDS TLS remains separately unverified. * Expanded MDS syslog setup with destination-capacity checks, isolated test and restoration steps, receipt-time searches and packet-level troubleshooting. Added Mac/VPN receiver instructions covering address changes, TLS identity and cleanup; live MDS delivery and mutual TLS remain separate qualification checks. * Protected new ACI events from reserved metadata collisions by preserving device attributes such as index\=1, 2 or 3 under vendor-prefixed names. Historical JSON index attributes remain available as vendor_index. Removed the global calculated index field because it can suppress exact-sourcetype event retrieval even when indexed counts are present. Existing raw data is unchanged; historical records can still expose vendor index values during automatic extraction. Use an explicit, search-local bucket-derived display field when investigating those older records; do not redefine the reserved index field globally. * Fixed Complete MDS monitoring setup rejecting valid end-port inventories above 1,000 records. The bounded readiness check now allows up to 50,000 records and tests the zones endpoint separately from VSAN inventory. Zoning pagination now follows the configured record limit instead of stopping at 10,000 records, and validates NDFC page-range metadata. Limited coverage is shown before creation; independent zoning feeds continue when another feed fails, with degraded health and the previous complete-success checkpoint preserved. * Fixed MDS monitoring setup rejecting the supported aggregate-alarm fallback. Readiness now shows all ten datasets and their blocking reasons, distinguishes safety-limit failures from unsupported response formats, and explains how to select a supported subset without weakening collection checks. * Clarified Nexus Dashboard, including Nexus Dashboard SAN, ACI, Nexus 9000 switch and MDS switch collection paths. Corrected automatic account-discovery guidance, documented blank credentials and retry behavior, and separated account associations from overlapping dataset collection. Direct MDS API collection remains unavailable; existing NDFC SAN collection and independent MDS syslog are unchanged. * Made Syslog & audit navigation consistent across Nexus Dashboard, ACI, Nexus 9000 and MDS. Added an independent MDS workspace with full-window counts, recent switch messages, Fibre Channel context, configuration and authentication evidence, and receiver setup links. Existing ACI and Nexus 9000 section URLs remain compatible; MDS live sender validation remains separate. * Corrected direct ACI syslog header, fault/event and ACL packet fields, including nested affected-object paths and sender timestamp recognition. Added streamed ACL investigation and expanded Nexus 9000 Syslog & audit with all messages and authentication history. Quiet streams no longer appear stale; classic Nexus charts now count before display limits and retain native message/host/time fallbacks. Syslog Coverage avoids unrelated API checks while retaining separate indexed-delivery and receiver evidence. Syslog investigation dialogs no longer infer controller links or API scope from sender names. * Fixed enable and disable controls for TLS syslog listeners on Home and Configured Inputs. State changes verify the existing TLS stanza, update only its enabled state, refresh native TCP listeners and check the resulting state without restarting Splunk. Plain TCP, UDP and API inputs keep their existing request types. * Added a dedicated ACI Syslog workspace for full-window message counts, recent streamed messages and fault-transition history, separate from current API fault state. Expanded the classic ACI dashboard beyond legacy categories and corrected chart totals, raw-message fallbacks and time-scoped drilldowns. * Added a distinct Traffic Analytics dataset check to Inputs Health using its managed `cisco:dc:nd:operational` / `traffic_analytics` output. Dataset counts overlap sourcetype totals and do not increase product event volume. * Improved Nexus Dashboard endpoint and traffic drill-downs with native lifecycle, all reported switch/interface attachments, anomaly titles, affected IP/service/conversation evidence when reported, and contextual next steps. Removed synthetic anomaly Value counts and misleading endpoint success status. Simplified interface charts to paired rates/utilization, added paired Traffic Analytics Tx/Rx charts, and moved selected values above plots. Physical links now retain reported measurements across unambiguous fabric boundaries, including zero values and source scope evidence. * Added a Nexus Dashboard Syslog & audit workspace for native audit operations and streamed anomaly history. Syslog Coverage now separates local receiver configuration from indexed delivery across ND, Orchestrator, ACI, Nexus 9000 and MDS; corrected native TLS inventory, classic login searches, count limits and drilldowns. Corrected native Exporter label spacing so streamed anomaly titles, severities and state flags remain visible. * Corrected automatic upgrade startup recognition for collector records carrying controller version provenance and freshness metadata. Valid completed cycles now advance handover verification while untrusted or malformed records remain excluded. * Clarified the Setup & upgrade guide to distinguish automatic startup checks from older exact-preservation verification. Documented retained disabled policies and index-qualified replacement names when an existing input owns the default name. * Added a Major severity filter between Critical and Warning in the Needs attention queue, with a matching count and saved URL selection. * Shows the signal title in the Critical now triage list while keeping the affected object in Entity. Signals without a title use their reported ID or an explicit generic label. * Kept keyboard focus in the centralized upgrade review after manual status refresh and blocked conflicting actions while that refresh is in progress. * Corrected missing-input readback during disabled staging: Splunk can return empty input and configuration feeds instead of HTTP 404. Staging now treats that consistent absence as not found while retaining strict checks for inconsistent or duplicate responses. * Made the collector helper directory an explicit Python package so a co-installed add-on's common module cannot shadow it. This prevents the verified REST-handler import failure on the local Python 3.13 instance. * Centralized automatic upgrades for Nexus Dashboard, ACI and Nexus 9000 in Setup & upgrade, reusing the monitoring policy controls. Enabled-source coverage is reviewed before durable disabled staging, bounded handover and restart-safe recovery; retained originals support restore. Nexus Dashboard combines compatible datasets and Orchestrator functions, with new checkpoints and possible initial-lookback replay. Startup observations, collection errors and indexed delivery remain distinct; one small cycle audit is retained even with error-only logging. ACI now accepts the verified concrete EPG parent wrapper and rotates deferred work instead of repeatedly returning to the same starting class. * Corrected Nexus 9000 syslog event timestamps for direct NX-OS messages with explicit year and timezone, while retaining relay-wrapped, yearless and RFC 5424 dates. Expanded the TLS setup guide with certificate trust, VRF selection, prompt test messages and handshake-timeout diagnosis. New events use audit creationTime or the RFC 5424 timestamp, including UTC and fractional seconds. The ND Syslog dashboard includes native audit and system-anomaly tables, and security login/logout audits join authentication classification. Previously indexed event times are unchanged; restart the receiving Splunk instance to activate timestamp parsing changes. * ACI account lists retain timestamped overlap evidence while refreshing in the background, including when returning within the same browser session. Incomplete checks retain prior evidence with an explicit warning. Syslog setup for Nexus Dashboard, ACI and Nexus 9000 no longer requires an API account; API collection retains its account requirement. Existing listeners are unchanged. * Refined Nexus Dashboard investigation details with shared account-name resolution, sorting by visible labels, fabric-specific guidance and keyboard focus restoration for interface drilldowns. Paired Tx/Rx charts keep consistent series colors and line patterns, expose full-precision bit rates beside scaled values and use accessible pressed-state legend controls. * Interface operational state also uses existing protocol evidence with its own observation time, including native and legacy status/display-name fields. Account labels avoid repeated names, and chart cadence requires distinct repeated time intervals rather than identical gaps across different series. * Refined Nexus Dashboard investigation workflows: highlighted selected view controls, neutral inventory membership lines, ND account labels, and creation-first Connectivity Analysis. Fabric metric lists use fabric names instead of internal keys; details omit switch-only attributes and inherited status and endpoint lists expose searchable IP addresses. * Improved interface and Traffic Analytics charts with Tx/Rx comparison, readable rate units, selectable measurements, client/conversation history, regular-cadence connections and preserved data gaps. Interface details provide directional rate/utilization columns, reported operational state and interface search. * Organized endpoint lookup into attachment context, summary cards and collapsed evidence. Separated active anomalies from advisories and linked assurance cards to their actual conditions. Added traffic-related active anomaly counts independently of native performance scores; category trends remain available in the collapsed overview. * Added the Guided Journey **Setup & upgrade** screen, permanent menu access, versioned setup.conf completion and resumable administrator progress. Each dialog explains how to read the panel, its threshold limits, its available drill-down, and the exact source and selected scope. * Added **Download support bundle** to Data Collection Health and a support-only analyzer/importer with guided launchers and a local Dashboard Studio investigation view. The bounded browser export redacts secrets and records its searchable-data coverage; the standalone tool is maintained under `tools/support_bundle/` and is not included in the installable app. * Rebuilt Data Collection Health for all five products with aligned status panels, sortable paginated evidence, contextual information dialogs, product drilldowns, and current-tab or all-tab PDF preparation. * Made every Failing Inputs severity and message an accessible diagnostics drill-down. The dialog preserves the complete raw entry, translates recognized timeout, authentication, authorization, API-route, throttling, TLS, connectivity, remote-service, response-contract, and duplicate-ownership patterns into cautious plain-language guidance, recommends focused checks, and opens the exact host, stanza, source, and severity evidence in Splunk Search. * Separated REST-handler registration, locally visible configuration, collector runtime errors, ownership heartbeats, syslog coverage, and fleet-wide indexed freshness so one evidence layer is not mistaken for another. * Added interval-aware freshness thresholds and dampened product rollups so a single stale sourcetype does not incorrectly classify every stream for a multi-sourcetype product. * Distinguished quiet activity-driven datasets from collection failures by reconciling indexed-event age with current collector-cycle evidence. The event-volume chart now shows exact product and bucket values on hover or keyboard focus, abbreviates large display values, and opens each segment in Splunk Search. * Added a normalized collector-cycle runtime contract with status, duration, API-call, event, dataset, warning, and checkpoint evidence where the collector can prove those values. * Added sanitized ownership heartbeats with product, input, owner, and installed version/build identity without presenting a heartbeat as proof that the upstream product API is healthy. * Moved app-owned file logs under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/cisco_dc_networking/` while retaining recursive `_internal` visibility. ##### Search, event, and compatibility contracts * Added administrator-controlled search-scope macros for each product and a guarded **Search Scope & Acceleration** editor for destination indexes and `summariesonly` behavior. * Fixed shared search macros so Classic dashboards, saved searches, data models, and React drilldowns remain valid in generating-command, nested-search, and inline search contexts. * Normalized controller identity across Nexus Dashboard, ACI, and Nexus 9000 API events. Default HTTPS forms such as `controller` and `controller:443` resolve to one lowercased field value for newly collected and retained data, while meaningful non-default ports remain distinct; indexed `host` metadata remains the bare monitored-device identity. * Standardized valid vendor timestamp selection with safe collection-time fallback for Nexus Dashboard, ACI, and Nexus 9000 REST events. * Standardized indexed `host` and CIM `dvc` identity across all five API product collectors so new events identify the monitored endpoint rather than the Splunk collection tier. * Added evidence-backed event types, field aliases, tags, and CIM mappings while retaining established Cisco data models and their independent acceleration boundaries. * Converted new Nexus Dashboard Orchestrator events to flat JSON while preserving historical flattened fields and dual-format extraction for previously indexed tab-separated events. * Kept established account stanzas, modular-input kinds, REST endpoints, indexes, sourcetypes, saved searches, Classic dashboard routes, and retained indexed data compatible unless an operator completes an explicit migration or cleanup action. ##### Security, reliability, and release engineering * Kept encrypted secrets on the server. Account reads and collector events do not return passwords, tokens, private keys, or credential-shaped payload fields to the browser. * Added bounded **Test Connection** actions that authenticate and perform one product-specific read without saving or changing the account. * Added allow-listed GET contracts, response/page/record/event/time limits, redacted diagnostics, credential-parameter rejection, same-origin redirect protection, and isolated failure handling for new collectors. * Added local overlap guards and documented single-owner deployment requirements for managed policies; the app does not claim a distributed lease across Heavy Forwarders or cluster members. * Stopped shipping enabled customer input instances. A clean installation registers modular-input kinds and the disabled recovery scheduler but collects nothing until an operator confirms creation. * Added Python 3.13 runtime selection for Splunk Enterprise 10.2 and later while preserving Python 3 selection on earlier supported releases. * Reorganized the installable app under `package/`, made `package/VERSION` the single release-version authority, and added deterministic build, version stamping, package verification, and byte-reproducible archives. Production entry points now emit one canonical minified React bundle with third-party license notices retained inline, so repeated builds do not alternate bundle formats or create an extra license sidecar in the package. * Updated vendored runtime dependencies and CA material, removed unsupported or obsolete packaged assets, and added configuration, schema, collector, migration, search, UI, and artifact contract tests. ##### Notable corrections included in 2.0.0 * Corrected the guided Nexus 9000 logging class to `loggingFacility`. Existing managed plans retry that reviewed class only when the former `syslogFacility` request returns 400/404 with no additional query parameters. Explicit and Custom API targets retain their exact paths; authentication, service and transport failures remain visible. The replacement passed a bounded live target check on NX-OS 10.6(3). * Preserved ACI statistics progress across request limits and temporary failures. Collection resumes after successfully written object pages so large classes do not repeatedly starve later interfaces. Managed plans use their advertised interval-based time allowance, retain their request limit, and report unattempted or deferred classes as incomplete rather than completed. Existing health and historical checkpoint keys remain unchanged. * Allowed one same-origin trailing-slash canonical redirect for Orchestrator GETs without changing the operation or query parameters. External redirects, changed operations, changed queries and redirect loops remain rejected. Deferred the remaining Nexus 9000 CLI batch after a shared connection or HTTP authentication failure, preserving failed coverage and retrying on the next scheduled cycle; command-specific errors still allow unrelated commands to run. * Added bounded diagnostic codes for rejected Orchestrator redirects and the phase of ND managed-health persistence failures. Diagnostics do not log redirect targets, query values, or arbitrary exception messages, and do not weaken ownership or health validation. * Preserved verified historical global checkpoint ownership for Topology and Endpoint locator after these collectors changed to fabric scope. Current collection still requires the correct fabric scope; historical keys remain owned for health persistence and controlled retirement or rollback, without deleting or resetting existing collection progress. * Made Orchestrator user collection select controller-advertised v2/v1 routes independently of the Nexus Dashboard platform version. When its schema is unavailable, reviewed user routes use bounded GET checks and alternate only after 404/405; permission, throttling, service and malformed-response failures remain visible. Preserved v2 user fields with legacy field aliases, extracted metadata-bearing and bare record lists before dependent requests, and bounded authentication refresh. Recognized explicitly structured JSON models published under a wildcard media type and refreshed older discovery caches. Existing input settings, sourcetypes and audit checkpoint keys remain unchanged; installed controller coverage still requires verification. * Bounded concurrent React searches through complete result retrieval to reduce search-slot exhaustion. Splunk concurrency limits remain unchanged, and failed evidence queries remain visible. * Corrected collector queue percentages to use matching KB or element units, preserved measured zeroes and unavailable inventory, and displayed reported blocked counters separately from blocked flags. Incomplete flag evidence cannot produce a healthy zero total. * Added controller-validated security-impact requests for observed advisory IDs and fabric/date scope for endpoint-locator snapshots. Missing IDs, incomplete listings and child failures cannot advance ND progress. Repeated Flow permission or missing-route failures are bounded per fabric within a poll; failed windows remain available for retry. Numeric zero retries and empty API walks remain measured zeroes. * Replaced ACI history DN comparisons with bounded time ranges and complete-result checks. Single-timestamp pages require distinct-record and stable-total proof before acknowledgement, retaining saved progress and overlap IDs. On first use, history checkpoints upgrade to version 3; an older collector that only understands version 2 cannot resume that upgraded state. Controller access, service availability, due collection cycles and fresh indexed data still require verification after installation. * Rejected ambiguous recovery-watchdog enabled-state responses instead of treating them as successful activation. Protected migration still enables and verifies the watchdog on demand; clean installations keep it disabled until needed. * Kept unknown Nexus Dashboard controller versions blocked after a failed lookup is cached. Later collector checks revalidate the cached version without repeating discovery or changing supported version-specific routes. * Organized discovered Nexus 9000 Custom API classes by function and class family. Search includes category and family labels, and unknown families remain visible under Other classes. Grouping changes presentation only; endpoints still come from the switch. * Fixed Nexus 9000 Custom API discovery on switches whose object browser does not publish model metadata. The picker discovers active switch classes and clearly labels the inventory as partial, preserving ownership and access checks. Saved class inputs continue polling their exact endpoint even when no active instance appears in discovery. Controller connection failures now provide retry guidance without raw request details. * Fixed account lists failing when Splunk returned an unreadable stored credential. All product account pages now read masked settings without decrypting or rewriting passwords, and edits preserve omitted secrets. Credential reads isolate the requested account and reject incomplete records with a clear error. If a replacement password is supplied while its proxy is disabled, an unreadable old credential can be replaced; any unrecoverable proxy password is cleared. If proxy use is enabled, re-enter its password too. If Test Connection or collection still cannot read a saved credential, check the Splunk role's password-store access and the instance's ability to decrypt its stored passwords. * Fixed an ND/NDFC account-handler startup error that made the account list return an XML parsing error after the offline-save change. Added full account-entrypoint startup coverage. * Account creation and editing now save locally without testing controller reachability or credentials. Test Connection remains optional and does not block Save; required fields and encrypted secret storage are preserved. Saving an ND/NDFC account no longer discovers or creates APIC accounts automatically. * Fixed MDS Custom API creation incorrectly requiring managed-policy datasets and per-dataset schedules. Custom inputs use their selected endpoint and polling interval; managed policies retain schedule and readiness validation. * Fixed ACI Custom API catalogs that failed with an XML parsing error when APIC advertised thousands of classes. Large catalogs now travel in bounded pieces and are reassembled before selection, retaining every discovered class, ownership restriction, and access-check result. Incomplete responses are rejected instead of displaying a partial list. * Declares affected-node fields as multivalue in the Nexus Dashboard Anomalies and Advisories data-model datasets, preserving the source node arrays. * Corrects the managed Flow worker to use the controller-version API contract, preserves unified statistics through historical field aliases, honors server-capped pagination, and bounds repeated connection or service failures while retaining failed windows for retry. * Extends the Health, Systems, Statistics, and Nexus Dashboard data models with controller addresses, container/process metrics, and Orchestrator fields. Flow byte/packet/latency fields are numeric; Flow arrays and endpoint IP/interface fields retain multiple values. * Uses data models for Tenant Utilization, controller inventory and process metrics, and additional Orchestrator aggregations. Classic model searches include unsummarized events with valid acceleration, preventing summary lag or a model rebuild from hiding indexed records. Broader raw-event scanning may occur while summaries catch up. * Adds empty/error guidance across Classic dashboards and separate source-coverage messages for flows, syslog, containers, audit records, and schema health. Messages do not create synthetic chart values. Sites separates controller addresses from the APIC cluster connection, preserves cluster scope in drilldowns, and includes a keyboard-accessible Show controller links button. Flow Traffic sorts by its displayed timestamp; narrow layouts allow panels and guidance to wrap. * Corrects Classic Tenant Utilization to display reported tenant-level traffic rates without dropping data through unrelated joins, counting overlapping hierarchy totals, or assuming inherited interfaces run at 40G. * Restores Classic Network Topology links when remote hostname enrichment is unavailable by retaining the reported device identity. * Repairs Classic Controller Statistics joins when APIC inventory is reported as fabricNode instead of topSystem, preserving controller scope and existing CPU/memory samples. * Replaces the obsolete standalone Setup Guide and missing assets with links to the current combined-app guide and configuration workspace. * Applies Classic panel-guidance styling to rendered HTML content so Splunk retains its spacing, emphasis, and long-text wrapping. * Restores Orchestrator array fields used by Classic site health, controller inventory, and schema panels after the move to JSON events. * Restores Classic Interface Stats fields for existing nested records and new managed collection, counts distinct interfaces, and scopes Congestion selectors to valid controller/fabric/switch/interface combinations. * Fixes modern Nexus Dashboard Anomalies collection to use paginated individual records from the Analyze details API, preserving genuine IDs, affected nodes, categories, and vendor timestamps. Classic anomaly counts exclude historical aggregate summaries; All filters retain records without optional fields, and evidence-based guidance explains summary-only or missing-data windows. * Repaired the Classic Sites fabric lookup. Selecting a health value now provides an accessible Open fabric link, or explains that the selected time range has no supported controller. * Fixed settings-resource reads that produced repeated HTTP 500 responses in Home and Application Setup. * Fixed unnamed-resource POST behavior in migration and search-scope workflows and corrected policy edits that were incorrectly handled as duplicate creates. * Fixed ACI session isolation, bounded account-worker pressure, epoch timestamp interpretation, class overlap handling, and resumable class scheduling for large monitoring plans. * Fixed ACI historical collection to resume from successfully written source events, adopt legacy timestamp checkpoints, and retain the checkpoint collection declaration through app deployment. Bounded ordered requests, a five-minute identity overlap, and visible checkpoint failures replace controller-clock progress and silent failures. * Added observation timestamps and resumable page progress for current ACI health and active faults. Historical records use their original creation time; unchanged health observations remain available on later polls. Interrupted uncommitted pages and the first legacy overlap can still replay records. * Preserved original historical checkpoint identities during protected ACI plan consolidation and backout. Replacement plans retain the original keys and ownership locks; missing receipts, mapping drift, or pre-existing independent replacement checkpoints require review. * Fixed Nexus 9000 neighbor topology, multi-command component ownership, DME query validation, and grouped exact-class selection. * Fixed MDS/NDFC authentication reporting, fabric identity, SAN Analytics fabric recovery, inventory readiness, policy editing, congestion ingestion, and bounded alarm degradation reporting. * Fixed Nexus Dashboard Orchestrator serialization, software-history event shaping, migration continuity, Congestion review layout, recovery-row visibility, and retirement performance. * Fixed Nexus Dashboard fabric discovery so events without `fabricName` do not create a selectable **Null** command-center filter. * Fixed dashboard search macro regressions, ACI `tstats` host filtering, bucketed timecharts, source-type parsing, event-type index scope, saved-search thresholds, and lookup contracts. * Fixed default-input provisioning, account-dependent form states, proxy toggles, field resets, product icon routing, action alignment, responsive wrapping, and configured-input grouping. ##### Upgrade and compatibility notes * Back up the current app, local configuration, encrypted credentials, and app-owned KV Store collections before installing 2.0.0. A migration restore point protects one transaction and is not a replacement for that backup. * Install the App and Technical Add-on as one versioned package. Do not overlay only selected files. * Existing inputs continue unchanged until an operator explicitly creates, migrates, restores, retires, removes, enables, or disables a configuration. * Open **Setup & upgrade**, review each detected product, and choose **Review automatic upgrade**. You can also open **Configure Application** from Home and use **Review automatic upgrade** under **Upgrade existing monitoring**, without entering Setup. This entry appears for enabled earlier-release ND, ACI or Nexus 9000 inputs when account and input inventory are available; it invites review and does not establish migration eligibility. Coverage starts with enabled original inputs. Review policy settings if needed, then choose **Apply upgrade** once. A restore point is saved before disabled staging, existing work finishes before replacement activation, and recovery continues after closing the browser or restarting Splunk. Previous exact-preservation migration receipts remain under **Review previous protected migration**; **Review or repair setup** remains available for protected recovery. * Keep retained pre-upgrade inputs and the downloaded export through the operational soak and recovery window. Use **Show pre-upgrade and recovery inputs** when exact retained rows must be inspected. * New Hyperfabric and MDS/SAN collection is not enabled automatically. Create and test the required connection before creating a policy. * Review field-based searches that parse ACI or Orchestrator `_raw` punctuation. Named-field searches remain compatible across retained and new event formats. * Review product search-scope macros when data is stored outside the factory index scope. Review data-model acceleration before enabling `summariesonly`. * Restart during an approved maintenance window before the first Nexus Dashboard automatic handover after installation. The workflow checks that earlier workers have exited before relying on the installed drain guards. Other restart requirements reported by Splunk remain separate. * Already indexed events are not removed by migration backout, policy retirement, old-input cleanup, or configuration downgrade. ##### Supported boundaries and known limitations * Automatic handover requires proven app-owned local inputs on a supported standalone or heavy-forwarder collection instance with Unix file locks. Unowned, retained or incompatible collection that could overlap an automatic policy requires account review. Separate accounts, destination indexes and incompatible cadences remain separate. Older exact-preservation migration retains its discovery and contract checks. * Nexus Dashboard automatic upgrade combines compatible enabled-source datasets into an inventory-enrolling policy and compatible Orchestrator functions into one input. It uses new managed checkpoints; initial lookback can replay data. ACI reuses preserved history identities where supported. Retained originals and checkpoints are not deleted. Restoring previous monitoring can replay data collected since the handover. * Two fresh collection cycles establish replacement startup. Partial collection errors remain visible as degraded startup and a collection-health follow-up; they are not described as healthy or fully indexed. A failed startup or verification timeout restores original input states. One small INFO cycle audit is emitted even when ordinary diagnostics use an error-only level, without changing that configured level. * ACI and Nexus 9000 support first-class API collection plus externally delivered syslog. SNMP, gNMI/model-driven telemetry, NetFlow, and APIC WebSocket subscriptions remain optional external integrations. * MDS and SAN Analytics collection uses qualified NDFC SAN APIs; this release does not add direct standalone MDS switch collection or configure SAN Analytics on NDFC. * Hyperfabric and MDS managed policies must run on one active collection owner. Local overlap protection does not coordinate independently enabled copies across hosts. * Custom API discovery shows GET operations or object classes advertised by the selected controller. Hyperfabric uses the current official cloud API publication. Availability depends on permissions, enabled services, and supported response/pagination contracts; missing or incomplete metadata is reported explicitly. * Generated Dashboard Studio views are retained only as migration references and are not promoted as supported replacements for the established Classic dashboards.


Description:
The Cisco Data Center Networking App delivers a comprehensive solution for data onboarding and visualization tailored to Cisco Data Center Networking products, including Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches, Cisco ACI, and Cisco Nexus Dashboard. It also enhances cross-correlation capabilities across data platforms by utilizing a unified index and application structure. Centralized Monitoring: Offers real-time monitoring of Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches, Cisco ACI fabrics, and Cisco Nexus Dashboard, providing detailed insights into anomalies and advisories with specific information about affected network objects. Customizable Dashboards: Includes a default dashboard optimized for faster loading using Base Search. Additionally, users can create personalized views to meet their specific requirements, ensuring critical data is easily accessible.

Release Notes:
First Splunkbase release. \- udp, tcp, syslog_udp, syslog_tcp and file transports, for any data diode or unidirectional gateway \- A separate key per OT site (stream_keys), reloaded without restart \- Reed-Solomon reassembly, late-frame handling and duplicate suppression \- Gap events with the replay command; frames in flight at shutdown reported as receiver_restart gaps \- Stream name conflict detection


Short Description:
Receives Splunk events sent one way across any data diode or unidirectional gateway by Diode Bridge Sender, over UDP, TCP, syslog or files. Verifies every frame, rebuilds lost data, drops duplicates, reports gaps, and indexes each event with its original index, host, source, sourcetype and time.


Description:
OT networks in power plants, refineries and other critical sites are often separated from IT by a data diode, which only lets traffic flow one way. Splunk-to-Splunk forwarding cannot cross a diode, because it needs acknowledgements sent back from the receiving side. Diode Bridge Receiver is the IT half of Diode Bridge. It runs on the heavy forwarder behind the diode and listens on the diode's output. It turns what Diode Bridge Sender sent from the OT side back into the original Splunk events, with the same index, host, source, sourcetype, raw text and _time. Nothing can be sent back across the diode, so the receiver works out by itself what arrived. It checks an HMAC-SHA256 signature on every frame and rebuilds lost data from Reed-Solomon parity. It accepts late frames and drops duplicates. Any frame still missing is reported as a gap, with the exact command to re-send it from the OT side. It is vendor-neutral and works with any data diode or unidirectional gateway that passes UDP, TCP, syslog or files. It takes any number of OT sites, each with its own key.

Sigma2SPL converts Sigma detection rules into Splunk SPL from inside Splunk Web. Detection engineers and SOC analysts paste Sigma rules as text, pick a field mapping, and get a ready-to-run search for every rule, without leaving Splunk or using an external converter. Paste one rule or up to 500 rules (2,000,000 characters) at once, separated by a line containing only ---. Each rule is converted on its own, so a broken rule never stops the others. When a rule cannot be converted, Sigma2SPL shows the line number, the offending line, the reason and how to fix it. Misspelled modifiers get a "did you mean" suggestion. Four field mappings are available. Windows uses the sources, field names and EventCode of the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows and Sysmon. Correlation rules (event count, value count, temporal) are supported when the rules they refer to are pasted in the same batch. All converted searches can be downloaded as a savedsearches.conf file in which every search is disabled and unscheduled until reviewed. Sigma2SPL runs entirely on the search head and needs no internet access. Rules are not stored, rule content is not logged, and the app never runs searches or writes configuration by itself.

item.description:

Release Notes:

Short Description:
Validates Splunk .conf files in your browser against version specs and SVA/best-practice rules - files never leave your machine. Flags unknown keys, security gaps, and cross-server parity issues across uploaded servers. Export findings to CSV and a topology diagram.


Description:
The Config Validator App validates Splunk configuration files against version specifications and best-practice rules entirely within the user's web browser. Uploaded files never leave the machine, and secret-shaped values such as passwords and keys are masked before anything is displayed or exported. Splunk configuration files are plain text with no built-in validation. An unknown key, a wrong value type, or an out-of-range value can reach production and surface later as a confusing restart failure or quiet misbehavior. Best-practice and security gaps accumulate across the servers in a deployment, and catching them by hand means reading config files against version-specific specs and comparing servers one by one. The app runs three layers of checks. First, conformance to the published .conf.spec sources for the selected version, plus a reviewed acceptance list of keys Splunk honors that the spec files omit. Second, curated rules drawn from Splunk Validated Architectures (SVA), best-practice guidance, required settings, and security hardening. Third, cross-server consistency checks that find parity issues across the uploaded servers. You upload individual .conf files or archived sets in .zip, .tgz, .tar.gz, or .tar format, and choose the target platform version (9.0.0 through 10.6.0.5). Findings appear with a severity of fail, warn, or info, grouped by rule with the affected servers listed. You can filter and drill into findings, export the filtered set to CSV, and view an interactive topology diagram of the servers and their relationships, exportable to SVG or draw.io. The app provides two operational modes: an embedded view within Splunk Web and a standalone page that runs outside of Splunk Web. Because no backend infrastructure or indexer connectivity is required, it deploys and is usable immediately after installation, with no additional configuration or data ingestion setup. It installs on Splunk Enterprise 10.x (tested on 10.2.1) and can validate configurations for 9.x platforms. Please note, using the app does not replace the btool commands to validate the configuration against your specific instance and is always a recommended step before running in this validator.

Nine distributable streaming commands: urlparse (registered domain, subdomain and public suffix from a bundled offline Public Suffix List), entropy (DGA and random-string hunting), similarity (typosquat and lookalike-domain detection with homoglyph folding), decode (base64, hex, URL and PowerShell -EncodedCommand), jwtdecode, ipclass (private, public, CGNAT, IPv6 ranges and your own CIDR lists), defang / refang and hashit. Free honeypot threat intelligence for Splunk. Enrich the IP addresses in your events with a verdict, ASN, ports and first and last seen, index free threat feeds of exploiter IPs and malware URLs, and query the honeypot dataset by CVE, payload, network, or JA4, Akin and HASSH fingerprint. Description:
HoneyLabs Intelligence is a free Splunk app for honeypot threat intelligence. It enriches the IP addresses in your own events with what HoneyLabs honeypot sensors recorded from them, indexes free threat feeds of active exploiter IP addresses and malware download URLs, and queries the honeypot dataset by port, payload, CVE, network, and JA4, Akin or HASSH fingerprint. HoneyLabs runs honeypot sensors on the public internet. No real user has a reason to connect to them, so the traffic they record comes from scanners, brute-force tools and exploit attempts looking for exposed systems. An address reaches the exploiter feed only when a sensor captured it running an exploit or a loader command, and known research scanners are left out. Every indicator links to its evidence at honeylabs.net/lookup. Getting started needs no account. Open the app's Setup page and turn on the threat feeds with one click each. Each feed is pulled every hour and needs no API key. The Triage dashboard then matches your traffic against them and lists hosts in your network that contacted captured malware infrastructure, followed by inbound connections from addresses seen running exploits. The honeylabs command enriches any event that carries a public IPv4 address: index=firewall | honeylabs field=src_ip | where honeylabs_events > 0 It adds a verdict, first and last seen, country, ASN and network owner, reverse DNS, the ports the address targeted and its exploit hits, each field prefixed honeylabs_. Addresses are de-duplicated per search, so a scanner that appears in ten thousand events costs one lookup. The honeylabssearch command queries the honeypot dataset directly. Its modes cover raw sensor events, captured request payloads, top attackers, timelines, IP, CIDR and domain lookups, CVE exploitation, ASN profiles, and fingerprint activity and population. Use it to see who else probes a CVE, what payload they send, or which sources share a JA4 fingerprint. The feeds and enrichment work without an account, and anonymous enrichment allows 10 lookups a day. A free API key from honeylabs.net raises that to 500 credits a day and is required for honeylabssearch and the Explorer dashboard. Pro allows 50,000 credits a day and Team 500,000. The key is stored through Splunk's storage/passwords, encrypted at rest and never written to a .conf file. A lookup sends only the public IP addresses in the field you name. Private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses are filtered out before the request is built, and no other part of the event leaves your deployment. The feed inputs are plain HTTPS downloads and send nothing about your data. With Splunk Enterprise Security, load the same feeds through the ES threat intelligence framework so indicators reach correlation searches and risk scoring. The guide at honeylabs.net/integrations/splunk-es has the field mappings.

Description:
TA-IPMI is a free, source-available Splunk add-on that brings out-of-band hardware health monitoring to any Splunk host with a server-class BMC. It reads full IPMI telemetry via ipmitool's local open interface and indexes it three ways with zero manual configuration: 1. Sensor readings: every SDR sensor (temperatures, fan RPM, voltages such as 12V/3.3V/Vcore/BAT, power draw in watts, plus thresholds), plus chassis and BMC status as rich JSON events (index=main, sourcetype ipmi:status) for fielded search. 2. Why it matters: IPMI/BMC is the only observability layer that survives OS crashes, power loss, and hangs. Overheating servers, dead fans, failing PSUs, dropped redundancy and unexpected reboots happen below the OS where agents and syslog can't follow, but the BMC remembers everything. TA-IPMI closes that blind spot in minutes: install it on the host, and its BMC telemetry flows into Splunk with ready-made overview and trend dashboards. Release Notes:
## SCIP v1.2.18 — Role-Aware Gateway Content, Prompt-Injection Pattern Accuracy, and OSV Range Matching This release supersedes v1.2.17 and carries forty fixes and improvements across AI and LLM threat detection, vulnerability matching accuracy, and deployment documentation. No configuration changes or manual steps are required on upgrade. No detection severity value or MITRE ATLAS technique mapping changed. **AI and LLM gateway coverage:** - Kong AI Gateway request payloads are now parsed and routed by message role across all three of Kong's logging key layouts, so prompt content is separated into user, system, assistant and tool channels instead of being evaluated as one blended string. - Kong AI Gateway responses now reach the role-aware assistant channel. Three response-reading detections, including LLM Sensitive Information Disclosure, previously returned nothing at all on Kong traffic. - user_input is assembled per message role on every supported gateway, so a detection targeting user-supplied prompt content no longer matches on system or assistant text. - LiteLLM deployments behind a load balancer now attribute activity to the real caller when the documented IP-forwarding step is configured. That documented step previously had no effect and attribution fell back to the balancer. - Gateway attribution fields are normalised consistently across the supported gateways, and the gateways where a field is not yet established are recorded as such rather than assumed. **Detection accuracy:** - Six detection stanzas no longer match on bare over-broad words such as "override" and "disregard", which fired on ordinary operational text. They now match the injection shape plus a tiered set of retained literals. - Prompt-injection patterns now match every "verb + qualifier + previous instructions" phrasing rather than a fixed list of phrases. - Two detections were rewritten away from literal phrase matching to shape-based patterns. - The credential-harvesting detection no longer fires on ordinary security advice. - Repeated injection attempts by one actor within one session no longer raise duplicate alerts. - LLM Cache Poisoning can now fire, because its gate read fields the rule never received. - Two detections carried pattern alternatives that could never match. Both are corrected, with regression fixtures added. - 68 ATLAS detections now surface the confidence value they already computed, bringing all 75 that compute one to carry it through to the alert. **Vulnerability matching:** - Advisories that express several affected version ranges for one package are now matched against every range. Previously only the first range was kept, so a component inside any later range was reported as not vulnerable. - Exact affected-version lists are now read for advisories that carry no machine-readable range. - Git commit hashes are no longer presented as upgrade targets, and the fix-availability state now distinguishes "no fix published" from "fix recorded only as a commit". - The bundled vulnerability seed and the live OSV feed both now cover all eleven documented ecosystems. The seed previously drew from five and the live feed polled eight. - Repository-qualified ecosystem values no longer reach the lookup. All three writers normalise the value, and an affected install corrects itself on its next scheduled run. - Severity grading in the bundled seed is restored. The offline generator carried an older severity parser that graded roughly 90 percent of rows as unknown. - The bundled snapshot date shown on the Home dashboard is written alongside the seed, so it can no longer report a date the seed does not match. - On licensed tiers the live OSV feed hands off to the vulnerability lookup automatically once it holds data, with no manual step. The Home dashboard freshness indicator derives its state from the lookup contents and adds a "lookup behind live feed" state. **Platform and documentation:** - The vendored Splunk SDK for Python is upgraded to 3.0.1. - Supported Splunk version statements are aligned across the app and its documentation. - The air-gapped and IL deployment guides are corrected. The OSV feed is now listed in the egress-disable procedure, the customer seed refresh procedure specifies the extraction rules it previously omitted, and the stated Python requirement for the offline seed generator is corrected. **Upgrade notes:** - No manual steps, configuration changes or saved-search edits are required. - Component vulnerability counts may rise after upgrade. Advisories with several affected version ranges were previously matched against the first range only, so components inside a later range were reported as not vulnerable. Those components now match correctly. Risk scores, dashboard counts and remediation rows reflect the corrected matching. - Installs running the live OSV feed on a licensed tier correct the ecosystem value in the lookup on the next scheduled run. No licensing or crypto surface was modified in this release. bin/scip_license_core.py and bin/scip_ed25519_verify.py are byte-identical to baseline.


Short Description:
A Splunk app that detects AI-threat patterns (MITRE ATLAS) and runs software composition analysis (SCA) on your SBOMs to identify known-vulnerable components (NVD, OSV) — surfacing the applications where both appear at once. Compliance evidence across nine frameworks and FedRAMP/RMF audit exports, with no separate platform to stand up.


Description:
SCIP is a Splunk app that detects adversarial AI/ML threats (MITRE ATLAS) and runs software composition analysis (SCA) on your SBOMs to identify known-vulnerable components (NVD, OSV) — then, through Compound Risk, surfaces the applications where an AI-threat detection and a known vulnerability appear at once, the exposure neither signal shows alone. It prioritizes with CISA KEV and EPSS and assesses compliance posture across nine frameworks — detection logic written as transparent SPL you can open and read, and no separate platform to stand up. AI THREAT DETECTION - MITRE ATLAS Detection — 81 AI/agentic threat detection rules (72 mapped to 57 MITRE ATLAS techniques) - Compound Risk — correlates MITRE ATLAS AI-threat detections with KEV-listed or critical-severity vulnerabilities on the same application - Silent-Source Detection — alerts when an enrolled AI/LLM telemetry source goes quiet, so a dead pipe is never mistaken for a clean one - AI/ML Bill of Materials — catalogs AI/ML model components from your SBOMs with insecure-serialization-format flagging and risk classification SOFTWARE SUPPLY CHAIN - SBOM ingestion — file-drop or HEC, supporting CycloneDX (JSON/XML) and SPDX (JSON) - Vulnerability correlation — bundled OSV dataset (250,000+ records across 11 ecosystems) with PURL-based correlation, refreshed daily from the live OSV feed across 8 configurable ecosystems; NVD CPE-based correlation; CISA KEV matching; EPSS scoring - Supply Chain Risk Score — 0–100 global and per-application scoring weighted by severity, KEV status, and EPSS - Vendor Risk — per-vendor risk aggregation and letter-grading - SBOM Drift Detection — baseline-vs-current component change tracking - Long-Unpatched Critical Exposure — flags critical/high-severity vulnerabilities unpatched 180+ days - License Compliance — GPL/AGPL/copyleft detection and license-risk classification COMPLIANCE, FEDERAL & AIR-GAPPED DEPLOYMENT - Air-gapped operation — AI-threat detection runs on your own Splunk data, SBOM correlation on the bundled OSV dataset, and intelligence feeds refresh by file transfer rather than live calls; deployed disconnected, SCIP makes no outbound connections - Compliance Gap Assessment — nine frameworks: PCI DSS 4.0.1, NIST CSF 2.0, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA Security Rule, EU Cyber Resilience Act, FedRAMP / RMF / CISA, DORA, FDA 524B Premarket Cybersecurity, SEBI CSCRF - POA&M & FedRAMP Workflow — POA&M dashboard, monthly ConMon package builder, BOD 26-04 risk-tier classification, deviation request workflow. Dashboards always available; automated POA&M generation is opt-in from Setup - Coverage-Evidence Manifest — AU-12-aligned attestation of unbroken AI-monitoring coverage - Audit-ready exports — FedRAMP POA&M Workbook, SSP Appendix M Integrated Inventory, Deviation Request Form

item.title: AssetDB - v1.6.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
### 1.6.0 #### Breaking changes in 1.6.0 Read these before upgrading from 1.5.7 or earlier. * **Splunk 10.2 or later is required.** The merge command now needs Python 3.13, which older versions cannot use for search commands. Upgrade Splunk first. * **Your merge search is updated on your first save.** After upgrading, scheduled runs keep using the old search until you save something on the Configure page (for example, change a setting and save). Run *Run preview* on the Pipeline tab before the next scheduled run to see what will change. * **You may get fewer, larger assets.** Earlier versions silently failed to join records that were far apart in a large input. They now join. * **Some data is skipped by default.** A key found in more than 50 rows is no longer used for matching, and a built-in list of placeholder values (for example `0.0.0.0`, `unknown`, `n/a`, all-zero MAC addresses) is ignored in key fields. Change both in Settings. * **Bad runs are blocked.** A run that produces fewer than half of the last run's assets is not saved, and a run with no assets never replaces the asset list. If your inventory legitimately shrinks by more than half, lower *Minimum size vs last run*. * **Multivalue fields keep the most recent values.** When a field has more values than *Max values*, it used to keep the first ones alphabetically. Set *Value order* to *Alphabetical* to get the old result. *Max values* is now limited to 1 to 100. * **Fill null works differently.** It now fills only assets that have no value in any source. Before, it competed with real values. * **Keep original case** cannot be combined with the host name, FQDN, user name, email or operating system normalizers. Change one of the two if a field uses both. * **Five macros are removed:** `retain_adb_lookup`, `ageout_adb_lookup`, `join_mv_fields`, `split_mv_fields` and `host_from_dns`. The merge did not use them. If your own searches do, copy their definitions from version 1.5.7. * **Two macros behave differently.** `input_adb_lookup` also sets `source_lookup`, and `normalize_mac` now returns lowercase. * **Only `admin` can change the app.** The `power` role could change app-level objects before. * **The Search entry is gone from the app menu.** Use the Search app. * **The asset list has new columns:** `source`, `source_lookup`, `last_seen`, `scope` and `conflicts`. Existing columns are unchanged, and your existing field configuration still works. #### New * A rewritten Configure page: Sources, Fields, Pipeline and Settings tabs, a status strip, and edits that are saved only when you click *Save*. * *Run preview*: see how many assets a run would add, remove or change before you run it. * Run history, with counts for each run and the groups that were too big to merge. * Options for sources (role, scope, max row age, row filter, field mapping) and for fields (normalizers, validation, ignore lists, merge methods, conflict flags). * Scoped keys, so the same address in two sites does not merge. * Safety checks: key blocklist, *Max rows per key*, and blocking of runs that look wrong. * A CIM preset for the standard asset fields, and macros to add asset details to events (`adb_enrich` and related). * Seven disabled saved searches that build source lookups. * A new app icon and logo, and help text in tooltips. * A faster merge (about 45% on a large test input).


Short Description:
Merges asset records from multiple lookup sources into a unified database by linking records that share MAC addresses, IP addresses, or hostnames.


Description:
AssetDB combines asset records from several lookups into one list of assets. Records that share an identifier, such as a MAC address, an IP address or a host name, become one asset, and their fields are merged. You can search the result and use it to add asset details to your events. It does not need Splunk Enterprise Security.

Dashboards that match on D3FEND tactic names or IDs in drilldown tokens need updating (for example `d3f:Harden`) - ATT&CK v20 replaced the Enterprise tactic *Defense Evasion* with *Stealth* and *Defense Impairment*; drilldowns that match on that name need updating - The default panel height is 1200 pixels (it was 2700) - Panels that are too small now scroll instead of squeezing the columns - *Sort by* now defaults to Value, Descending - The entrance animation is always on, once when the panel first loads - The legend title is always the value field's name; the menu is smaller and grouped into Data, Display, Colors, Scale and Export **Removed** - The *Theme* option (the heatmap follows the dashboard's theme), the *Animate* and *Duration* options, *Legend title*, and the sweeping highlight animation **Fixed** - Enterprise tactic order for v20, several heatmaps on one dashboard affecting each other, *Hide empty* removing sub-techniques that have values, zero and decimal values in tooltips, searching for names that contain `&`, one click sending several drilldowns, and several platform choices that showed an empty matrix - Text built from field names in the legend is now escaped


Short Description:

Description:
The MITRE ATT&CK Heatmap for Splunk is a custom visualization that transforms search results into interactive MITRE ATT&CK or D3FEND matrices. The visualization colors each technique based on numeric values returned by a search query, enabling security teams to visualize detection coverage, identify gaps, and highlight areas of concentrated activity. The app supports the ATT&CK Enterprise, ICS, and Mobile frameworks, as well as the D3FEND framework. It ships with bundled matrix data (ATT&CK v20.0 and D3FEND v1.6.0) and includes an optional scripted input that automatically imports newer ATT&CK versions from the MITRE GitHub repository. The visualization integrates with both Simple XML and Dashboard Studio, providing drilldown capabilities and export options. Users format the heatmap by selecting the framework, domain, color scale bounds, and whether to use bundled or imported matrix data.
